why: An optional call f?.(x) inside a callback, where f is a function the enclosing function received (a parameter, or a const naming one). The callback is a unit of its own whose captured inputs are its parameters (callbackEnvironment), and a plain call f(x) there is admitted. optionalCallShape (lower.mjs) read locality through common.mjs originOf, which does not know callback inputs, so the lint refused the optional form: 'an optional call reads a local function value'. The lint and the translator now give optionalCallShape the function that declares f as its locality scope when f is an immutable captured input of the callback (optionalScope). Before: the lint refused parent.ts, theorem not generated. notifyAll and notifyLater are unchanged or refactored around an identical callback; notifyNamed names the callback with a const first. notifyNext passes x + 1: lane B witnesses. notifyProp calls a function field of a captured record (h.onItem?.(x)), read the same way through the record path; notifyPropNext doubles x: lane B witnesses. The proof rows rest on the spec/theorem.py split_top fix for arrow types (497cc8c8).
